ledger.note: 1924: Feng Yuxiang seizes Beijing. 'he switched sides and seized the capital in the Beijing Coup on 23 October 1924'; 'Feng renamed his army the Guominjun or the National People's Army' (undated); the Guominjun page: 'formed when Feng betrayed the Zhili clique during the Second Zhili-Fengtian War'. The Second Zhili-Fengtian page gives 22 October.

November 1924 (bridging): 'It had control of much of Northwestern China, including Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan' (Guominjun page, undated); the Second Zhili-Fengtian War ended with 'a Zhili loss of all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun' (war page), and the Zhili clique held Chahar and Suiyuan from 1922 (its own page), so the transfer is placed at the war's end on a reading. Mirror of the zhili-clique loss of Chahar and Suiyuan, 1924-11. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: Chahar and Suiyuan split out of the 1925 gain and dated to November 1924 to match the Zhili dossier; confidence 1.]

1925 (bridging): 'It had control of much of Northwestern China, including Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan'; the page gives no date and no former holder (the anhui-clique dossier lists Shaanxi among the provinces Zhili annexed), so the year and the counterpart are readings. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: Chahar and Suiyuan moved to their own event (1924-11).]

Late 1925: the Anti-Fengtian War. 'In late 1925, Fengtian general Guo Songling defected to the KMC; this sparked the Anti-Fengtian War against Zhang Zuolin' (month not given; the Fengtian page dates Guo's rebellion to November 1925). The zone is the researcher's reading.
January 1926: the Guominjun is beaten. 'Feng was defeated by a Zhili-Fengtian alliance in the Anti-Fengtian War in January 1926.'

January 1926: Beijing is lost. 'He lost control of Beijing and retreated to Zhangjiakou, where his army became known as the Northwest Army.' The Zhang Zuolin page has Zhang capturing Beijing in June 1926, so who held it in between is not on the pages.

1927: Feng Yuxiang takes the governorship of Gansu. The Muslim conflict in Gansu page (1927-1930, opened 2026-10-25): 'The position of Gansu governor was taken by Feng Yuxiang' and 'many of the non-Muslim warlords were expelled by Liu Yufen's Guominjun army of 15,000 soldiers' (the page's spelling); the Gansu page: 'The Muslim Conflict in Gansu (1927-1930) was a conflict against the Guominjun'; the Central Plains War page then names 'Gansu, Shaanxi and Henan' as Feng's provinces in 1930. The year is the conflict's start year and the exact month is not on any page; the counterpart 'nobody' stands for the expelled non-Muslim warlords (no state). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added; the first version said Gansu was not on the pages.]

28 May 1927: the Guominjun takes Luoyang and Henan. Northern Expedition page (re-read 2026-10-25): 'Feng Yuxiang and his Guominjun moved first, leaving their base in Shaanxi to march on Luoyang, in Henan'; 'On 28 May, Li took Suzhou, while the Guominjun took Luoyang, forcing Zhang Zongchang to withdraw his forces to Shandong, and Zhang Xueliang to fall back north of the Yellow River'; 'Following Xueliang's retreat, Feng Yuxiang moved east from Luoyang to Zhengzhou'. Henan as a whole is a reading (Wuhan's Tang Shengzhi attacked in Henan the same month, and Fengtian forces were there 'in support of Wu Peifu'); the counterpart is Wu Peifu's Zhili clique. Mirror of the zhili-clique loss of Henan, 1927-5. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added; the first version omitted Henan, which the page names.]

The first review round proposed 1927-5; the page puts the allegiance in June and the land in May (the kuomintang dossier's own note says the same). notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from four pages. Cliopatria has no Guominjun row. The pages are thin: the Guominjun page gives no dated territory, and the Feng page gives only the coup, the January 1926 defeat, the 1926 Soviet trip, and July 1927. Not settled: (1) the extent and dates of the Guominjun's holdings in the north-west (Shaanxi, Chahar, Suiyuan: one undated sentence; Gansu, Ningxia and Henan are not on the pages, though the Republic of China dossier puts the Guominjun in Shaanxi and Henan in 1930); (2) the Nankou campaign of 1926, the Wuyuan oath of September 1926 and Henan 1927 are not on the pages; (3) the coup date, 22 or 23 October 1924; (4) who held Beijing from January to June 1926; (5) the end: the pages give the 4 November 1930 resignations, not a dissolution of the Guominjun; (6) the Guominjun page's infobox has no active years. A gap-filler should open '1924 Beijing Coup', 'Nankou Campaign' and 'Hu Jingyi'. Gazetteer: all names resolved; Chahar and Suiyuan are Inner Mongol rings.

[ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, after the adversarial review (verdict fail)] (1) Gansu and Henan: the first version said they were not on the pages; the Central Plains War page names them and the Northern Expedition page dates Luoyang (28 May 1927). Added a Henan gain from zhili-clique (1927-5, confidence 2, mirror of the zhili-clique loss) and a Gansu gain (1927, confidence 2, counterpart 'nobody': the Muslim conflict in Gansu page, which no earlier version had opened, gives Feng Yuxiang the Gansu governorship and dates the conflict 1927-1930; no page gives a month), and split the 1926-1930 keyframe into guominjun_1926 (1926) and guominjun_1927 (1927-1930, with Gansu and Henan). (2) Vassal events added from the vassal's side: kuomintang 1927-6 to 1929-12 and republic-of-china 1930 to 1930-5. I put the start in June, not May as the review proposed: the Northern Expedition page dates Feng's alignment with Nanjing about 20 June 1927 and the land to May. (3) Chahar and Suiyuan: the transfer from Zhili is now dated November 1924 (confidence 1) to match the zhili-clique dossier's split of its November 1924 loss. (4) The Northern Expedition is added to the wars with a Henan zone. (5) Not settled, and the pages the review pointed to do not settle it: when Shaanxi, Chahar and Suiyuan were taken, and what happened to Chahar and Suiyuan after the January 1926 retreat. The Anti-Fengtian War page (opened) is silent on all four provinces; Chahar and Suiyuan stay in the 1927-1930 shape at confidence 1 although the Central Plains War page lists only Gansu, Shaanxi and Henan. (6) The counterpart fix of the first round (dissolve to republic-of-china) stands and the dissolve land now includes Gansu and Henan. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25, area check of the review] Cliopatria has a row 'Anti-Kuomintang Coalition' (slug anti-kuomintang-coalition, 1930-1931, about 556,635 km2, group ea-08) that overlaps this dossier's shape in 1930 and is not mentioned in the first version: the row is the Central Plains War coalition of Yan Xishan, Feng Yuxiang and Li Zongren as one polity, and this dossier draws the Shanxi/Guominjun share of it; the renderer should draw the coalition row or the two dossiers, not both. No infobox area exists on the pages opened to compare.
